name: goat_horn
revision: r1 (2026-11-10): first draft from the writers' room pitch (rank 3, develop just) with the critic's fixes applied
caption: my dad vs this goat: 0 wins, 212 losses 🐐
logline: A kid whose dad gets rammed off the same cliff by the same goat every day finds out what Dad was really after the morning Dad leaves for the far mines.
question: why tf does my dad let a goat knock him off a cliff every day?
premise: A goat on the shelf above the lake has knocked Dad off the same cliff 212 times. He lands in the deep lake, climbs the stairs back up, and stands in front of it again, one step in front of a big oak, trying to dodge at the last second so the goat hits the oak. He's too slow. Old Ida next door has a goat horn on her wall and says a goat missed her once. Dad's donkey is packed for the far mines for the winter, and he said he can't go without one thing, his kid thinks it's revenge. This morning Dad left anyway.
twist: Dad wasn't losing a grudge match. A goat drops a goat horn only when it rams a solid block, never a player, so Dad was trying to make it miss him and hit the oak: a horn for his kid, to call him from anywhere while he's away (a goat horn is heard 256 blocks off). The kid takes Dad's spot, steps on the goat's tell, the goat hits the oak, out pops a GOAT HORN, he blows it, and far down the road Dad turns around.

requests.direction: A sunny mountain morning. A bubbly nine-year-old kid tells a friend a funny story about his dad and a goat: fast, bright, full volume, a grin in it, a short breath between sentences.
A sunny mountain morning. A bubbly nine-year-old kid tells a friend a funny story about his dad and a goat: fast, bright, full volume, a grin in it, a short breath between sentences.
A mountain lake. A big gruff dad, soaked to the skin, shouts a score up a cliff to his kid: full volume, cheerful, proud of it.

lines.text: A GOAT / has knocked / my DAD / off the same CLIFF / 212 TIMES.
lines.say: A goat has knocked my dad off the same cliff two hundred twelve times.
lines.direction: one quick excited breath, already laughing at it, lean on the number

lines.text: He lands / in the LAKE / and climbs / BACK up.
lines.direction: bright and matter-of-fact, like it's the most normal thing in the world

lines.text: He tries / to DODGE / so it hits / the OAK. / Too SLOW.
lines.say: He tries to dodge so it hits the oak. <short pause> Too slow.
lines.direction: fond and teasing, the last two words flat and quick, a little wince
shouted up from the water, cheerful and proud, like a high score

lines.text: Old IDA / has a GOAT HORN. / She says a goat / MISSED her once. / Goats don't MISS.
lines.say: Old Ida has a goat horn. She says a goat missed her once. <short pause> Goats don't miss.
lines.direction: gossipy and sure of himself, the last sentence a know-it-all shrug

lines.text: Dad's DONKEY / is packed / for the far MINES. / ALL winter.
lines.say: Dad's donkey is packed for the far mines. <short pause> All winter.
lines.direction: the energy dips, the last two words smaller, but still full volume

lines.text: Dad SAID / he can't go / without ONE thing. / I figured / it was REVENGE.
lines.say: Dad said he can't go without one thing. <short pause> I figured it was revenge.
lines.direction: bouncing back to funny, a dramatic little drop on the last word

lines.text: And this morning, / he LEFT anyway.
lines.direction: the one sad line: plain and quiet in feeling, still full volume, no whisper

lines.text: So I took / his SPOT. / FOR him.
lines.say: So I took his spot. <short pause> For him.
lines.direction: a breath, then determined and proud

lines.text: It dropped / its HEAD. / I STEPPED.
lines.say: It dropped its head. <short pause> I stepped.
lines.direction: fast and tense, each sentence a beat, the last word snapped

lines.text: BONK. / Right into / the OAK. / Out popped / a GOAT HORN.
lines.say: Bonk! <short pause> Right into the oak. Out popped a goat horn.
lines.direction: the first word a big comic sound, then amazed, rising to the last two words

lines.text: It was / for ME. / I BLASTED it.
lines.say: It was for me. <short pause> I blasted it.
lines.direction: the penny drops: a beat of wonder on the first sentence, then a huge happy grin

lines.text: Way down / the ROAD, / Dad TURNED / AROUND.
lines.direction: bursting with joy, the last word held a moment

beats: S13 holds under 1 s after 'AROUND': Dad, back to us, waving at the far cliff, the horn's call still ringing, cut
ending.loop: cause and effect: the 212 knocks in L01 were 212 tries at this horn
